profile.reading:
This is Digital Realty facility SJC11, at 3011 Lafayette Street, Santa Clara, CA 95054. Digital Realty's own property listing for SJC11, fetched this session, lists the building at 91,000 square feet.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building sits within Digital Realty's Silicon Valley campus, a dense cluster of buildings across Santa Clara and Santa Clara County that is one of the company's oldest US footprints, reflecting the area's history as a birthplace of the commercial colocation and internet exchange industry. Digital Realty's own Silicon Valley metro page, fetched this session, lists numerous named properties concentrated along Comstock Street, Lafayette Street, and Walsh Avenue, ranging from under 15,000 to nearly 400,000 square feet each. The company does not publish a consolidated IT power rating in megawatts for individual Silicon Valley buildings in the sources reviewed this session.

Digital Realty markets its Silicon Valley properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning the metro alongside Northern Virginia, Chicago, Dallas, and New York/New Jersey, all tracked elsewhere in this registry, as core hubs in its global interconnection and colocation platform. The company's FY2025 10-K identifies the United States as its largest single national market by both facility count and rentable square footage.

reading.body:
Digital Realty SJC11 is a 91,000 square foot building at 3011 Lafayette Street in Santa Clara, California, one of dozens of individual properties Digital Realty operates in Silicon Valley under its PlatformDIGITAL brand. The operator does not publish an IT power capacity in megawatts for this building, either on its property page or in its Form 10-K filing; without a disclosed power rating, the building's relevance to AI infrastructure scaling cannot be determined from available facts.

This facility sits within Silicon Valley's dense cluster of colocation properties, a region served by PG&E where large hyperscaler campuses and legacy colocation tenants compete for grid capacity and cooling resources. California has published power capacity at only 11 of its 103 mapped data center facilities this site has tracked, totaling 365 MW across the state, reflecting the industry's general reluctance to disclose per-building specifications. Without power data for SJC11, it ranks outside the state's measurable capacity footprint.

The absence of a published megawatt figure for an individual Digital Realty property is typical of the company's disclosure practice; as a landlord rather than operator, it reports aggregate portfolio metrics to the SEC rather than building-level power specs. Whether SJC11 matters to AI compute growth depends on its tenant mix and power density, neither of which is published by the operator and therefore not knowable from the sources reviewed.
